title: Finite cofinal resolution with embedded nondegenerate simplices
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets, constant diagrams and right-pinched Kan mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with universes enlarged as necessary. A finite simplicial set means one with finitely many nondegenerate simplices; a simplex is nondegenerate when it is not obtained by a nonidentity surjective simplex operator from a lower-dimensional simplex. A monomorphism means a simplicial map injective in every degree. For every finite simplicial set $X$ there exist a finite simplicial set $Q$ and a map $q:Q\to X$ such that every nondegenerate simplex $\Delta^n\to Q$ is a monomorphism and, for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, map $p:X\to\mathcal E$ and vertex $T\in\mathcal E$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_XT)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\mathcal E)}(pq,\Delta_QT).$$
The case $X=\varnothing$ is allowed with $Q=\varnothing$. No quasicategory hypothesis on $X$ or $Q$ and no colimit-existence assumption on $\mathcal E$ is made.

proof.text: HTT Variant 4.2.3.16's induction requires a lift $\partial\Delta^n\to Q_0$ through a cofinal $Q_0\to X_0$ that is not supplied. Cofinality does not imply this: the final-vertex inclusion $\Delta^0\to\Delta^1$ is cofinal, but the endpoint map $\partial\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$ does not lift through it. We use Kerodon 02MQ's pullback-and-cone correction of that construction. Call a simplicial set nonsingular when all its nondegenerate simplex maps are monomorphisms. Induct on the total number of nondegenerate simplices to prove the stronger assertion that every finite $X$ has a finite nonsingular $Q$ with a universally localizing $q:Q\to X$ [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. Identities are universally localizing, since all their pullbacks are identities and their restriction functors are identities, with the collection $W$ empty. For $X=\varnothing$ choose the identity of $\varnothing$, which is finite and nonsingular; its cocone restriction is the identity required by the item.

proof.text: For nonempty finite $X$, choose a maximal-dimensional nondegenerate simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$. Remove exactly its degeneracies, obtaining $X_0$. This is a simplicial subset: write a remaining simplex as a degeneracy of $\tau\ne\sigma$ by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition]. Applying an operator factors through a face of $\tau$; a proper face has dimension less than $\dim\tau\le n$ and cannot have ancestor $\sigma$, whereas an improper face retains ancestor $\tau$. A simplex of $X_0$ degenerate in $X$ has its ancestor in $X_0$, by applying a section of its surjective degeneracy operator. Thus $X_0$ is finite with exactly one fewer nondegenerate simplex. Its degrees below $n$ agree with $X$; degree $n$ adds only $\sigma$; and all higher simplices are degenerate. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-glue-simplex] to obtain $X=X_0\amalg_B D$, where $B=\partial\Delta^n$ and $D=\Delta^n$. The boundary map $B\hookrightarrow D$ is degreewise injective. By the strengthened induction hypothesis choose a finite nonsingular $A$ and a universally localizing $a:A\to X_0$.

proof.text:
Put $H=B\times_{X_0}A$, with projections $b:H\to B$ and $r:H\to A$. The map $b$ is universally localizing directly from the definition: for every $T\to B$, $T\times_BH=T\times_{X_0}A$, with the same projection and localization data. Define $C=H\star\Delta^0$ as the right cone, and write $j:H\hookrightarrow C$ for its initial-block inclusion. In degree $m$, $C_m=H_m\amalg\{*\}\amalg\coprod_{s+t+1=m}H_s\times\{*\}_t$, with operators restricting the initial $H$ block and final apex block. Define graph embeddings $i_A=(r,j):H\to A\times C$ and $i_D=((B\hookrightarrow D)b,j):H\to D\times C$. Each is injective because its second coordinate $j$ is injective. The maps $a\operatorname{pr}_A:A\times C\to X_0$, $b:H\to B$ and $\operatorname{pr}_D:D\times C\to D$ give a strictly commuting map of spans, by the pullback equation $ar=(B\to X_0)b$. Consequently the degreewise pushout defines an actual map
$$q:Q=(A\times C)\amalg_H(D\times C)\longrightarrow X_0\amalg_B D=X.$$
All attaching maps are defined on $H$; no boundary lift has been assumed.

proof.text: Nonsingularity passes to simplicial subsets: the ancestor of a simplex is obtained by a face section of its degeneracy surjection, so the subset has the same nondegenerate simplices as the ambient set within it. It passes to binary products as follows. Write the components of a nondegenerate $m$-simplex $(x,y)$ as $\bar x\alpha,\bar y\beta$ for monotone surjections $\alpha,\beta$, using [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition]. They cannot both repeat any consecutive pair of indices, or the pair would be degenerate. Thus the monotone pair $i\mapsto(\alpha(i),\beta(i))$ is injective: equality at two distinct indices forces repetition on all intervening consecutive pairs. Since $\bar x,\bar y$ are embeddings, this gives a degreewise injective simplex map for $(x,y)$. Both $B,D$ are nonsingular, since their nondegenerate simplices are injective ordinal maps. Thus $H\subseteq B\times A$ is nonsingular. The cone $C$ is nonsingular: its mixed nondegenerate simplex is a nondegenerate simplex of $H$ followed by the distinct apex. The associated map is injective on the pure and mixed blocks, which are disjoint in the displayed join formula. Hence $A\times C$ and $D\times C$ are nonsingular. The two graph inclusions are injections, so each factor embeds in $Q$: degreewise, their pushout identifies only the two copies of the common subset. Every simplex of $Q$ lies in one factor; if nondegenerate in $Q$, it is nondegenerate in that factor. Its standard simplex map is therefore a composite of two injections. This proves that $Q$ is nonsingular.

proof.text: We verify finiteness. A subset of a finite simplicial set has only finitely many nondegenerate simplices by the ancestor argument in step 4. Each degree of a finite simplicial set is finite, since [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] encodes its degree-$m$ simplices by a nondegenerate ancestor and a surjection out of $[m]$. If $U,V$ are finite of dimensions at most $d,e$, a nondegenerate simplex of their product has dimension at most $d+e$: in the two component degeneracy surjections at least one index must increase at each consecutive pair, as in step 4. Product degree sets are finite and there are only these finitely many possible nondegenerate degrees. Thus $B\times A$, and its subset $H$, are finite. The cone adds just the apex and a mixed nondegenerate simplex for each nondegenerate simplex of $H$, so $C$ is finite, including $H$ empty. Thus both product factors of $Q$ are finite. Each nondegenerate simplex of $Q$ has a preimage in one of them, and that preimage cannot be degenerate. The two finite lists therefore surject onto the nondegenerate simplices of $Q$.

proof.text: The cone $C$ is weakly contractible, including $H=\varnothing$: its realization contracts to the apex by multiplying the coordinates on its $H$ block by $1-t$ and adding their lost mass to the apex coordinate. This simplexwise formula respects face and degeneracy identifications and descends continuously to the quotient. Apply [lem-coef-contractible-factor-universal-localization] to $a:A\to X_0$ and $C$, and to $1_D$ and $C$. It gives the two outer vertical universal localizations $A\times C\to X_0$ and $D\times C\to D$. The middle map $b$ is universally localizing by step 3. Apply [lem-coef-universal-localization-pushout] with its subscript-0 side taken to be $D\times C\to D$. Its monomorphism hypotheses are precisely $H\hookrightarrow D\times C$ and $B\hookrightarrow D$, established in steps 2–3. It concludes that the induced $q:Q\to X$ is universally localizing. Steps 4–5 prove the other two clauses of the strengthened induction, completing it.

proof.text: Take the base change of $q$ along $1_X$ in [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. For each quasicategory $\mathcal E$, restriction is a functor equivalence from $\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)$ to a full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\mathcal E)$. It induces equivalences on mapping spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The inclusion of the full subcategory has exactly the same right-pinched mapping spaces between its objects: each simplex of such a map has only those objects as vertices. Apply this to $p$ and $\Delta_XT$. Restriction sends them exactly to $pq$ and $\Delta_QT$, because precomposition preserves constants degreewise. Hence the induced equivalence is restriction itself, the map in the item. Both mapping spaces are Kan by the same calculus. No colimits in $\mathcal E$ and no quasicategory hypotheses on either indexing simplicial set have been used.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_embedded_simplex_resolution {X : SSet.{u}} [X.Finite] : ∃ (Q : SSet.{u}) (_ : Q.Finite) (_ : Q.Nonsingular) (q : Q ⟶ X), ∀ (E : SSet.{u}) (_ : E.Quasicategory) (p : X ⟶ E) (T : E _⦋0⦌), SSet.Enhanced.IsFunctorEquivalence (SSet.Enhanced.mappingSpaceMap ((MonoidalClosed.pre q).app E) (SSet.Enhanced.diagramVertex p) ((SSet.Enhanced.constantDiagrams X E).app _ T))
